findings.name: Cynthia
findings.detail: Champion of the Sinnoh League. Team is not mono-typed — deliberately diverse (no two Pokémon share a type), signature Pokémon is Garchomp. First female non-playable Champion in the core series.
findings.trackable: Hall of Fame registration after defeating her; Elite Four/Champion can be rechallenged afterward, with her team's levels increasing (up to level 77-79) after the player completes the Stark Mountain postgame story event.

findings.name: Cyrus
findings.detail: Leader of Team Galactic. Fought mandatorily twice: (1) at Team Galactic HQ in Veilstone City after infiltrating it — on defeat he gives the player a Master Ball and allows the lake guardians to be freed; (2) at Spear Pillar after he summons Dialga (BD) with the Red Chain — the lake trio arrives and destroys the chain before/during this fight, freeing Dialga. Cyrus is defeated, rages, retreats/vanishes (in the original DP lore he disappears through a rift; the full 'Distortion World' portal sequence is a Platinum-exclusive expansion).
findings.trackable: Story-flag only; no dedicated boss-kill counter observed.

findings.name: Commander Mars
findings.detail: Mandatory battles: (1) Valley Windworks (Route 205 area), (2) Lake Verity, (3) Spear Pillar — fought as a 2v2 Multi Battle alongside Commander Jupiter (player + rival Barry vs. Mars + Jupiter), stalling the player while Cyrus summons Dialga.

findings.name: Commander Jupiter
findings.detail: Mandatory battles: (1) Team Galactic Eterna Building (top floor), (2) Spear Pillar — 2v2 Multi Battle with Mars against player + Barry.

findings.name: Commander Saturn
findings.detail: Mandatory battles: (1) Lake Valor (inside Azelf's cave), (2) Team Galactic HQ in Veilstone (overseeing the imprisoned lake guardians / Red Chain creation). Unlike Mars and Jupiter, no source confirms a Saturn appearance at Spear Pillar itself.

findings.name: Lake guardians (Uxie, Mesprit, Azelf)
findings.detail: Uxie = Lake Acuity, Mesprit = Lake Verity, Azelf = Lake Valor. Each is captured by Team Galactic early on (mandatory story beats at each lake), then freed as part of the mandatory Spear Pillar climax where they destroy the Red Chain. Catching the trio afterward is OPTIONAL, not required for story progress: Uxie and Azelf can be caught in their lake caverns, while Mesprit becomes a roaming encounter that flees the region until engaged/caught (missable in the sense that it roams and can be difficult to pin down, though it does not permanently vanish).

findings.name: Dialga
findings.detail: VERSION EXCLUSIVE TO BRILLIANT DIAMOND (Pearl/Shining Pearl instead summons Palkia). Summoned by Cyrus at Spear Pillar via the Red Chain; after Cyrus's defeat and the chain's destruction by the lake trio, the player has the opportunity to battle and catch Dialga at level 47 (per general DP/BDSP legendary encounter conventions — exact level not independently confirmed this session) directly at Spear Pillar as part of/immediately following the story climax.
findings.trackable: Pokédex entry; also whether it's in the party/box.
sources: Bulbapedia - Pokémon Brilliant Diamond and Shining Pearl

findings.name: Team Galactic HQ infiltration / Cyrus first battle
findings.detail: Located in Veilstone City. Player infiltrates using a Galactic Key card, confronts Saturn, then Cyrus, who afterward hands over a Master Ball and permits release of the lake guardians.

findings.name: Spear Pillar climax
findings.detail: Final Team Galactic confrontation atop Mt. Coronet. Sequence: player fights through Grunts, then a 2v2 Multi Battle vs. Mars+Jupiter (with rival Barry as partner), then Cyrus summons Dialga/Palkia with the Red Chain, the lake guardian trio arrives and destroys the chain, Cyrus battles the player one final time and is defeated, then retreats/vanishes. Player can then catch the freed legendary.

findings.name: Sinnoh League Champion victory / Hall of Fame
findings.detail: Defeating Elite Four (Aaron, Bertha, Flint, Lucian in that order) then Champion Cynthia registers the player in the Hall of Fame, the primary 'ending' trigger of the main campaign.
findings.trackable: Hall of Fame entry; save file / trainer card presumably marks Champion status (not independently confirmed this session).

findings.name: Stark Mountain / Heatran (Buck questline)
findings.detail: Postgame-only location, accessible after Hall of Fame. Rival Barry appears at the entrance; NPC Buck accompanies the player through the cavern to retrieve the Magma Stone, after which Heatran (level 70) becomes catchable in its chamber after talking to Buck's grandfather in the Survival Area. IMPORTANT VERSION NOTE: unlike Pokémon Platinum, this sequence in Diamond/Pearl and Brilliant Diamond/Shining Pearl does NOT involve Team Galactic or the character Charon — that subplot (Charon leading remnants of Team Galactic, Looker arresting him at Stark Mountain) is Platinum-exclusive and does not exist in Brilliant Diamond.
findings.trackable: Pokédex entry for Heatran; completing this event is reported (single source, unverified independently) to be the trigger that raises the Elite Four/Champion's rematch levels.

findings.name: Turnback Cave / Giratina
findings.detail: Located north-central Sendoff Spring; accessible only after entering the Hall of Fame. A maze with a fixed entrance room and fixed Giratina room; the rooms in between are randomized each visit. Giratina (Altered Forme) appears at level 70; if defeated or fled, it respawns on next Hall-of-Fame-postgame visit. NOTE: This is a simple single-room legendary encounter, NOT the multi-area 'Distortion World' dungeon featured in Pokémon Platinum's mid-story — Brilliant Diamond does not have the Distortion World as a location; Giratina is Turnback-Cave-only.

findings.name: Elite Four / Cynthia rematch
findings.detail: Elite Four and Champion can be rechallenged after Hall of Fame entry; their Pokémon levels increase once the player completes the Stark Mountain story content (Cynthia's team reported to reach level 77-79 post-Stark-Mountain vs. lower levels beforehand). No evidence found of a separate roaming/route rematch with Cynthia outside the League itself (as exists with some other postgame champions in other Pokémon titles).
findings.trackable: Implicit via being able to re-enter the League and refight the same trainers.

findings.name: Looker (International Police investigator)
findings.detail: Appears repeatedly during the Team Galactic campaign arc (Jubilife City, Valley Windworks, Eterna Building, Galactic Warehouse, Team Galactic HQ) helping the player. In Platinum his postgame arc culminates in arresting Charon at Stark Mountain, but since Charon does not appear as a character in Brilliant Diamond/Shining Pearl (replaced by a generic Team Galactic Grunt, with Charon only referenced via notebook flavor text in Rotom's Room), it is UNCONFIRMED whether/how Looker's postgame arc concludes in Brilliant Diamond specifically.

findings.name: Single ending, no branching
findings.detail: No evidence found of multiple endings or narrative branches in Brilliant Diamond; the Hall of Fame registration after beating Cynthia functions as the game's 'ending' beat, consistent with mainline Pokémon campaign structure. Could not find an explicit description of end-credits content or post-credits epilogue text this session.

versionNotes.note: Dialga is exclusive to Brilliant Diamond as the Spear Pillar legendary; Shining Pearl gets Palkia instead. This mirrors the original Diamond/Pearl split.
Brilliant Diamond/Shining Pearl follow the original Diamond/Pearl gym order (Maylene 3rd, Fantina 5th), NOT Pokémon Platinum's reordered sequence (which swaps Fantina to 3rd).

The Distortion World as a multi-room dungeon (mid-story Giratina confrontation with Cynthia) is Platinum-exclusive and does not exist in Brilliant Diamond; BD's only Giratina encounter is the postgame Turnback Cave single-room fight.

Charon does not appear as a character in Brilliant Diamond (replaced with a generic Grunt sprite; only referenced via notebook text), unlike Platinum where he becomes a significant post-Cyrus antagonist confronted by Looker at Stark Mountain. This subplot is effectively absent in BD.
Stark Mountain in Brilliant Diamond (as in the original Diamond/Pearl) is a pure Heatran-catching sidequest with Buck — it does NOT include the Team Galactic/Charon confrontation that Platinum added.
